name: ImageSchemaNet index (for Ampharos)
derived_from: ImageSchemaNet (isnet_correct.owl) in github.com/StenDoipanni/ISAAC, by Stefano De Giorgis et al. Aligns FrameNet, VerbNet, WordNet and MetaNet to image schemas.
license: No license file in the repository as of 2026-10-01. Treat as research data: fine for internal reference; ask the authors before redistributing.
coverage: Six image schemas: SOURCE_PATH_GOAL, BLOCKAGE, CONTAINMENT, PART_WHOLE, CENTER_PERIPHERY, SUPPORT. Other schemas (VERTICALITY, BALANCE, LINK...) are not covered; use motif_sourcing.translate_schema for those.
how_to_use: Take the key verbs and nouns of the feeling and the copy. Look each up in `words` (lemma, lowercase) to see which schema and which role it activates. The role tells where the subject sits and what the line builds; read `prism` for how that role is drawn. `frames` does the same for FrameNet situations, with each frame element's role.

SOURCE_PATH_GOAL.line: a path line with a start and an end

roles.SOURCE: where the line starts; the subject's history or the problem side
roles.PATH: the line itself; its treatment (wandering, solid, dashed) tells how the journey goes
roles.GOAL: the outcome end; where the ray is

BLOCKAGE.line: a wall line across the path, or a pinch

roles.BLOCKER: the wall or the pinched point (vocabulary.states.pinched); never the rounded square
roles.BLOCKED: the subject stopped at the wall; no ray until it is past

CONTAINMENT.line: a closed run of lines, or a ray as scope (relations.held_within)

roles.CONTAINER: the closed line or the scope ray
roles.INSIDE: the subject within it; trapped if closed lines, sheltered if a scope ray

PART_WHOLE.line: units on a grid; complete vs broken

roles.PART: a unit (hexagon) or a gap in one
roles.WHOLE: the complete structure; lit when finished

CENTER_PERIPHERY.line: radial arrangement; faint edges, crisp center

roles.CENTER: the subject, where the ray focuses or highlights
roles.PERIPHERY: faint or unlit elements at the edge (lit_vs_unlit)

SUPPORT.line: a span or base line beneath the subject

roles.SUPPORTER: the span, grid, or a rounded square beneath
